Answer: A
Reason: The chest radiograph shows a large right-sided pleural effusion causing near-complete opacification (white-out) of the right hemithorax. The significant mass effect from this fluid accumulation pushes the mediastinum and trachea to the contralateral (left) side, which is the classic presentation for a massive pleural effusion compared to atelectasis (which would pull the mediastinum ipsilaterally).
